page_meta.title: Hyperlipidemia Refills Online in California | TeleDirectMD
page_meta.description: Refill cholesterol medications online in California. Board-certified Family Medicine MD. CA telehealth law compliant. Aetna in-network. Self pay $79. ACC/AHA 2018 cholesterol + 2022 update. Statin tier framework. GoodRx CA pricing.
page_meta.icd10_display: E78.5 (Hyperlipidemia, unspecified), E78.0 (Pure hypercholesterolemia) — final coding per clinical details

opener.text: California adults with established hyperlipidemia can refill cholesterol-lowering medications — including statins, ezetimibe, and fibrates — by secure video visit through TeleDirectMD, consistent with California Business and Professions Code Section 2290.5. A California-licensed board-certified Family Medicine physician reviews your most recent fasting lipid panel, LDL-C level, 10-year ASCVD risk score, and statin tolerance before authorizing refills. The ACC/AHA 2018 Cholesterol Guideline, supplemented by the 2022 ACC Expert Consensus on Non-Statin Therapies, guides therapeutic decisions. Self pay is $79. Aetna is in-network effective April 30, 2026.

epidemiology.ca_prevalence: High cholesterol (LDL-C ≥130 mg/dL or total cholesterol ≥240 mg/dL) affects approximately 29% of California adults — about 9 million people — per CHIS 2022 data and CDPH chronic disease surveillance. Statin use in California is approximately 23% of adults over 45, reflecting both high disease burden and treatment gaps.
epidemiology.ascvd_burden: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in California, accounting for approximately 60,000 deaths annually per the CDPH Heart Disease and Stroke Prevention Program. Optimal LDL-C management remains a high-priority preventive intervention for California's population.
epidemiology.disparities: South Asian Californians have elevated ASCVD risk at lower BMI thresholds; Filipino Californians have higher rates of metabolic syndrome contributing to dyslipidemia. The ACC/AHA 2018 guideline identifies these populations as risk-enhancing factors warranting earlier statin initiation.

high_intensity.label: High-intensity statins
high_intensity.preferred_for: Established ASCVD (secondary prevention), LDL-C ≥190 mg/dL, T2DM with high ASCVD risk

moderate_intensity.label: Moderate-intensity statins
moderate_intensity.preferred_for: Primary prevention in lower-risk adults, statin-intolerant patients requiring dose reduction

low_intensity.label: Low-intensity statins
low_intensity.preferred_for: Statin intolerance requiring lower dose; typically added to ezetimibe

clinical_guidelines.nla_reference: National Lipid Association (NLA) guidelines support LDL-C and non-HDL-C targets, particularly for patients with elevated TG and complex risk profiles. TeleDirectMD applies ACC/AHA framework as primary guideline.
clinical_guidelines.ezetimibe_use: Ezetimibe added to statin therapy provides additional 18–24% LDL-C reduction. ACC/AHA 2022 expert consensus recommends adding ezetimibe when LDL-C remains ≥70 mg/dL on maximally tolerated statin for ASCVD patients.
clinical_guidelines.pcsk9_referral: PCSK9 inhibitors (evolocumab, alirocumab) are used for familial hypercholesterolemia or ASCVD patients with LDL-C ≥70 mg/dL despite maximum tolerated statin + ezetimibe. These require specialist (cardiologist or lipidologist) management and prior authorization — TeleDirectMD facilitates referral.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring: Fasting lipid panel annually for stable patients on statin therapy; CK and ALT/AST if myopathy symptoms develop. Physician reviews most recent lipid panel before refill.
clinical_guidelines.telehealth_scope: TeleDirectMD refills established statin and ezetimibe regimens for stable patients with recent lipid panel. Newly diagnosed severe hypercholesterolemia (LDL-C ≥190 mg/dL) may require in-person workup for familial hypercholesterolemia.

medications.name: Atorvastatin 10/20/40/80 mg
medications.notes: Most widely prescribed statin. High-intensity at 40–80 mg. Less CYP3A4 interaction than simvastatin.

medications.name: Rosuvastatin 5/10/20/40 mg
medications.notes: High-potency, fewer drug interactions than atorvastatin. Dose reduce to 5–10 mg if eGFR <30.

medications.name: Ezetimibe 10 mg
medications.notes: Added to statin for LDL-C not at goal. ~18–24% additional LDL-C reduction. ACC/AHA 2022 recommended add-on.

medications.name: Fenofibrate 48/54/145/160 mg
medications.notes: Used for hypertriglyceridemia (TG ≥500 mg/dL) or mixed dyslipidemia. Not primarily LDL-C lowering. Monitor LFTs and CK.

medications.name: Simvastatin 10/20/40 mg
medications.notes: Taken at bedtime for peak cholesterol synthesis coverage. Multiple drug interactions (e.g., amiodarone, diltiazem) — 80 mg dose FDA-restricted due to myopathy risk.

faqs.question: Can I refill my cholesterol medication online in California?
faqs.answer: Yes. California Business and Professions Code Section 2290.5 permits licensed physicians to prescribe appropriate medications via synchronous video telehealth. TeleDirectMD's California-licensed board-certified Family Medicine physician reviews your most recent fasting lipid panel, LDL-C level, 10-year ASCVD risk score, and statin tolerance before authorizing refills. Statins and ezetimibe are not controlled substances and can be prescribed via California telehealth. Self pay is $79; Aetna is in-network effective April 30, 2026.

faqs.question: What cholesterol medications can TeleDirectMD refill in California?
faqs.answer: TeleDirectMD refills established statin regimens (atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, simvastatin, pravastatin, lovastatin), ezetimibe, and fibrates (fenofibrate) for stable hyperlipidemia. Medication selection follows the ACC/AHA 2018 Cholesterol Guideline and 2022 Expert Consensus. PCSK9 inhibitors (evolocumab, alirocumab) require specialist management — TeleDirectMD will facilitate a cardiology or lipidology referral.

faqs.question: What is the difference between high-intensity and moderate-intensity statins?
faqs.answer: High-intensity statins — atorvastatin 40–80 mg and rosuvastatin 20–40 mg — reduce LDL-C by 50% or more and are preferred for established ASCVD (secondary prevention), LDL-C ≥190 mg/dL, and Type 2 diabetes with high cardiovascular risk. Moderate-intensity statins — atorvastatin 10–20 mg, rosuvastatin 5–10 mg, simvastatin 20–40 mg — reduce LDL-C by 30–49% and are used for primary prevention in lower-risk adults. The physician selects intensity based on your 10-year ASCVD risk score and LDL-C target.

faqs.question: How much do statin medications cost in California with GoodRx?
faqs.answer: Generic statins are among the most affordable prescription medications in California with GoodRx coupons. Atorvastatin 40 mg/month: approximately $5–$18. Rosuvastatin 20 mg/month: approximately $12–$30. Simvastatin 40 mg/month: approximately $5–$12. Ezetimibe 10 mg/month: approximately $12–$25. Fenofibrate: approximately $15–$35 per month. Prices as of May 2026 — actual prices vary by pharmacy location and dose.

faqs.question: What does my 10-year ASCVD risk score mean for statin therapy?
faqs.answer: The 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk score estimates your probability of a heart attack or stroke in the next decade, calculated using age, sex, race/ethnicity, total cholesterol, HDL, systolic blood pressure, BP treatment status, diabetes, and smoking history. Per ACC/AHA 2018 guidelines: ≥20% risk = very high-risk (high-intensity statin strongly recommended); 7.5–19.9% = intermediate-risk (statin benefit discussion recommended); 5–7.4% = borderline (risk-enhancing factors may justify statin); <5% = low-risk (focus on lifestyle). The physician calculates your ASCVD risk score at each visit.

faqs.question: Does California Medi-Cal cover statin medications?
faqs.answer: Medi-Cal covers generic statins including atorvastatin, simvastatin, pravastatin, and lovastatin at low or no cost-sharing under the Medi-Cal formulary. Rosuvastatin and ezetimibe are also covered with prior authorization in some managed care plans. However, TeleDirectMD is not currently enrolled as a Medi-Cal provider, so Medi-Cal will not cover TeleDirectMD visits. Medi-Cal members can use the $79 self-pay rate or seek care from a Medi-Cal-enrolled provider.

faqs.question: What labs do I need before a hyperlipidemia refill visit?
faqs.answer: The physician requires a fasting lipid panel (total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C, triglycerides, non-HDL-C) within the past 12 months before authorizing a statin refill. If you are on a statin plus fenofibrate, a comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP) with liver function tests is also reviewed. If you report muscle pain or weakness, creatine kinase (CK) testing is recommended before refill. Labs available at Quest Diagnostics, LabCorp, and community health clinics throughout California.

faqs.question: What should I do if I have muscle pain on a statin?
faqs.answer: Muscle pain (myalgia) is the most common reason for statin intolerance, affecting approximately 5–10% of statin users. If you develop new muscle pain while on a statin, the TeleDirectMD physician will review the severity, timing, and associated symptoms. Mild myalgia may be managed with dose reduction or switching to a different statin. Severe muscle pain with dark urine suggests rhabdomyolysis — a rare emergency requiring immediate in-person care and statin discontinuation. A creatine kinase (CK) lab check helps distinguish myalgia from serious myopathy.

faqs.question: When is ezetimibe recommended alongside a statin?
faqs.answer: The ACC/AHA 2022 Expert Consensus recommends adding ezetimibe when LDL-C remains ≥70 mg/dL (for ASCVD patients) or ≥100 mg/dL (for high-risk primary prevention) despite maximally tolerated statin therapy. Ezetimibe reduces intestinal cholesterol absorption and provides an additional 18–24% LDL-C reduction on top of statin therapy. Generic ezetimibe 10 mg is approximately $12–$25 per month with a GoodRx coupon at California pharmacies.

faqs.question: Does California telehealth parity law cover my cholesterol management visit?
faqs.answer: California Assembly Bill 744 (2019), codified in Insurance Code §10123.85, requires commercial health plans to reimburse telehealth services on the same basis as in-person care. Parity applies when TeleDirectMD is in-network with your plan. Aetna commercial (active April 30, 2026) and UnitedHealthcare Commercial (active May 29, 2026) are in-network in California. Anthem Blue Cross and Cigna are pending enrollment.

faqs.question: What lifestyle modifications complement statin therapy for hyperlipidemia?
faqs.answer: The ACC/AHA 2018 Cholesterol Guideline emphasizes lifestyle changes alongside medication: a heart-healthy diet (Mediterranean or DASH pattern, reducing saturated fat to <6% of total calories), regular aerobic exercise (150 minutes per week of moderate-intensity activity), smoking cessation, weight loss for overweight patients, and limiting alcohol. Diet and exercise alone can reduce LDL-C by 15–25%. The physician discusses lifestyle optimization alongside medication management at each refill visit.

faqs.question: Can I get PCSK9 inhibitor therapy refilled at TeleDirectMD in California?
faqs.answer: No. PCSK9 inhibitors — evolocumab (Repatha) and alirocumab (Praluent) — require specialist management, step therapy documentation, and prior authorization that exceeds the scope of a telehealth refill visit. If you are a candidate for PCSK9 inhibitor therapy (familial hypercholesterolemia or established ASCVD with LDL-C ≥70 mg/dL despite maximum tolerated statin + ezetimibe), TeleDirectMD will facilitate a referral to a cardiologist or lipidologist who can manage PCSK9 therapy and prior authorization.
